scope.summary: Author the bodykit_bodies (BDY-) and bodykit_recipes (BRC-) PostgreSQL migrations per Section 13.16 (BK-16.3 storage authority/canonical DDL): TEXT primary keys with prefixed uuid_v7, NOT NULL event_ledger_event_id per ARCH-036/TAI-OVR-014, and guard_authority_write(AuthorityMode::Postgres) required before every write. Bodies persist BodySpec authority state; recipes persist saved channel/skin/genital layer bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Migration creates bodykit_bodies (body_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY 'BDY-{uuid_v7}', body_spec_json JSONB NOT NULL, schema_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hsk.tailor.body_spec@1', created_at/updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ, event_ledger_event_id TEXT NOT NULL) and bodykit_recipes (recipe_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY 'BRC-{uuid_v7}', recipe_json JSONB NOT NULL, name TEXT, tags TEXT[], event_ledger_event_id TEXT NOT NULL).
Migration filename follows the dated convention (2026_07_08_tailor_bodykit_bodies_recipes.sql), applies cleanly on an empty database, and is idempotent-safe under the migration runner.
storage.rs write paths call guard_authority_write(AuthorityMode::Postgres) as their first statement; a test proves an insert without the guard fails closed.
CHECK constraints reject PKs not matching their 'BDY-'/'BRC-' prefix and reject NULL event_ledger_event_id.
scope.risk_if_missed: Body authority written without ledger linkage or the Postgres guard silently forks state from the EventLedger, destroying the replayability guarantee (TAI-OVR-007) that recipe reproducibility and audit depend on.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
